key_insight: MedCORE turns medical image diagnosis into criteria-based reasoning by localizing clinically meaningful signs, modeling how they relate, and weighting uncertain evidence less.
clinical_relevance: This could make image-based diagnoses more interpretable and closer to how clinicians assess morphology and texture across different imaging types.
method: Breaks each diagnosis into explicit clinical criteria and localizes them to relevant image regions
Uses multi-scale evidence encoding plus a graph attention network to model dependencies between criteria
Aligns image criteria with text descriptors, class prototypes, and uncertainty-calibrated aggregation
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on ISIC 2018, BUSI, and IDRiD, reaching 89.2%/96.1%/84.3% accuracy and strong F1/AUC results across all three datasets.
watch_item: Performance is promising, but real-world clinical use would still need validation for robustness, generalization, and reliability of the criterion explanations.
paper_title: MedCORE: Criteria-Grounded Clinical Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis
